message.content: In Christian tradition, the figure most often regarded as the central prophetic voice is Jesus Christ himself. Christians believe that Jesus fulfilled the prophetic expectations of the Hebrew Scriptures and that his teachings and life are the ultimate revelation of God’s will. However, the importance of other prophets—such as Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and others—is also emphasized in many Christian teachings, especially in the context of the Old Testament’s role in shaping the narrative that leads to Jesus. Because beliefs about who is “most important” can vary among denominations and individual believers, it is common to see a range of perspectives on this topic.
